description: Integration contract for the Student 2 RESOLVE IQ Intelligence Engine. Student 3 and Student 4 consume the OUTPUT schema only; they never need to read Student 2's Python internals.

input_schema.description: Payload accepted by main.analyze_complaints(complaints). Student 1's backend forwards raw complaints in exactly this shape.

complaint_id.description: Unique complaint identifier. Optional but STRONGLY recommended - the engine generates 'idx-<n>' when absent, which breaks cross-system joins.

text.description: Raw, unprocessed customer complaint text. REQUIRED. null/empty is tolerated and reported in diagnostics.warnings.

customer_id.description: Synthetic/opaque customer identifier. No personal data is stored by Student 2.

order_id.description: Order identifier used to join complaint intelligence back to orders.

created_at.description: Complaint date (ISO-8601, YYYY-MM-DD). Drives previous/current period trend split. Unparseable values are excluded from trend maths and reported in diagnostics.warnings.

output_schema.description: Return value of main.analyze_complaints(complaints). Guaranteed JSON-serialisable (json.dumps(result) always succeeds).

analyzed_complaints.description: One enriched record per input complaint, in input order.

clean_text.description: Preprocessed text (lowercase, punctuation removed, whitespace collapsed).

severity.description: See allowed_values.severity. PROJECT RULES, not universal severity.

cluster.description: Human-readable semantic cluster name derived from the dominant issue_type of the cluster.

embedding.description: L2-normalised sentence embedding. Length = metadata.embedding_dim (384 for all-MiniLM-L6-v2). Omit with include_embeddings=false.

trends.description: Per-issue volume and period-over-period growth, sorted by current volume descending.

current_count.description: Same as count; explicit for clarity.

growth_percent.description: ((current - previous) / previous) * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. previous=0 & current=0 -> 0.0; previous=0 & current>0 -> 100.0.

emerging_issues.description: Subset of trends whose growth_percent >= metadata.emerging_growth_threshold AND current_count >= metadata.emerging_min_count.

growth_threshold.description: Threshold that was applied for this run.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show in a dashboard tooltip.

clusters.description: Cluster summary for dashboards and legends.

periods_analyzed.description: Number of distinct calendar months seen (2 = previous + current).

embedding_backend.description: sentence-transformers | hashing-bow | null when embeddings failed.

diagnostics.description: Degradation is reported, never silently swallowed.

warnings.description: Recoverable per-record or backend issues (missing optional fields, unparseable dates, backend fallbacks).

errors.description: Stage failures that degraded the output (e.g. clustering unavailable).

student_1_backend.summary: Student 1 owns the API and authentication. It forwards raw complaints to main.analyze_complaints() and returns the resulting dict to Student 3 and Student 4.
student_1_backend.how_to_call: from main import analyze_complaints, load_complaints, save_output
student_1_backend.recommended_architecture: Run Student 2 as an in-process module or a small HTTP worker (POST /analyze with the input_schema, response = output_schema). Keep it stateless.

student_3_agent_should_not: Read Student 2's Python source or import classification/severity internals.
Re-implement severity, classification or trend maths - it is already done here.
student_4_dashboard_visualizes: analyzed_complaints[] -> filtered/paginated complaint table, severity badges, sentiment chips
trends[] -> bar chart (count per cluster_name) and line chart (growth_percent)
emerging_issues[] -> alert cards / emerging-issue banner with the 'reason' text
clusters[] -> donut/pie chart of cluster size and legend names
student_4_dashboard_should_not: Run embeddings, clustering or trend maths in the browser.
Depend on embedding vectors for basic views - they are optional (include_embeddings=false omits them).
integration_notes.json_validity: The engine asserts json.dumps(output, allow_nan=False) succeeds before returning; numpy scalars/arrays are converted to native Python types.
